transcript.answer: The OpenTelemetry metrics API, unlike its tracing API, has no proxy meter. An instrument created from `metrics.getMeter()` before a `MeterProvider` is registered is therefore permanently a no-op, and it stays one even if a provider is registered later. In Lore, `libs/server-core/src/outbound/otel.ts` created its instruments at import time. The entrypoint imported that file before `initOtel()` ran, so counters such as `lore.http.requests` and `lore.tool.calls` never recorded anything. ADR-050 and PR #2652 fixed this by moving the instruments to `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts`. That file looks each instrument up lazily on the global meter provider that is registered at record time, and memoizes the lookup per provider.

judgements.reason: The answer states that the metrics API has no proxy meter, that instruments created before provider registration stay no-op permanently, and that Lore resolves instruments lazily against the current provider; the added detail does not contradict the gold answer.
